subject: Ops handbook: BYO key flow and SSO risk treatment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>, Emma Park (Helio) <emma@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Ops handbook: BYO key flow and SSO risk treatment

Team — looping you in on Helio Health's request (attached) and the ask from sales to surface an "exception playbook" for customers requesting BYOK + shortened retention windows plus SSO provisioning guarantees. Key context: Helio is in discovery for Dedicated and they want a binding operational commitment for (1) BYOK handover steps, (2) 90-day audit log retention instead of our standard 365, and (3) SCIM/SSO provisioning SLA for 3rd-party IdP.

Helio's security sent the attached spreadsheet with required evidence and a list of gating questions. Sales (Ben) flagged this as a gating item to close a mid-six-figure commit (deal HL-2026-7781). I want to triage product + infra asks and come back with a proposed exception playbook we can present to their security team by EOW.

Questions to triage:
- Is a customer key import (PKCS#8 wrap) + HSM-admined key material acceptable from an infra standpoint? (Karthik)
- Can we document a smaller audit-log retention bucket (90 days) with controls for eDiscovery and legal holds? (So we don't break compliance for other customers)
- What SSO provisioning risk exists if SCIM propagation is slower (e.g., >30s) during high churn? Any mitigation?

Ask: Please add short bullets (3–4 lines) in reply with your recommended decision and any blockers. I attached a strawman playbook (proposed_playbook_draft.md) — use that to speed up. Also attaching Helio's sheet.

Attachments: helio_security_req.xlsx, proposed_playbook_draft.md

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>, Emma Park (Helio) <emma@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops handbook: BYO key flow and SSO risk treatment

Marcus — quick triage notes below (high level). I skimmed Helio's sheet and the proposed playbook. Attaching a short PDF with my annotations.

- Audit logs: 90-day retention is reasonable as an exception if we provide a read-only export window of 365 days to a customer-owned S3 for eDiscovery (we already have the export pipeline). Operational impact: +5% storage+ingest cost, and we need a small UI flag to mark "short retention" accounts to ensure routing through the export pipeline.
- BYOK: Customer-supplied key import (encrypted PKCS#8) into our HSM is feasible. Blockers: need a formal KMS onboarding checklist (crypto attestation + access policy), and a one-time manual KYC/ops step for key ownership verification. If Helio insists on customer-managed HSM that we cannot access, we must scope Private deployment only (can't support on Hosted/Dedicated).
- SSO/SCIM SLA: Propagation delays are the main risk for immediate access revocation. Mitigation: require session revocation TTL of 15 minutes for any exception accounts and enable an emergency "kill switch" for provisioning. Also recommend a scoped SCIM retry/backoff policy.

Decision recommendation (short):
1) Approve exception path: BYOK import into Redwood HSM with KYC + one-time ops verification.
2) Approve 90-day retention for Helio with mandatory 365-day export to customer S3 for legal holds.
3) Require SCIM SLA clause + session TTL of 15m and emergency disable in the playbook.

Notes: We'll need product to sign off on UI + flag work (Marcus) and infra to scope the HSM onboarding flow (Karthik).

Attachments: soojin_triage_notes.pdf

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example.com>, Emma Park (Helio) <emma@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops handbook: BYO key flow and SSO risk treatment

Adding technical constraints and a rough timeline from infra:

- BYOK import model: we support two flows — (A) wrapped import (customer encrypts key blob with our public wrapping key, we unwrap into HSM) and (B) remote wrap (customer-managed HSM that performs wrapping). Flow A is doable for Hosted/Dedicated after we add a one-time import validation + attestation step. Flow B forces Private-only (can't guarantee crypto quarantine on Hosted).
- HSM attestation: we need ~3 engineering sprints (6 weeks) to harden the import pipeline, build audit events, and automate key rotation policies for imported keys. Manual ops can be used short-term with strict runbooks but increases lead time (~2 weeks for onboarding).
- Audit log export: export-to-customer-S3 is implemented, but we need a small audit tag on records for shortened-retention accounts so the export job includes them. That's ~1 sprint (2 weeks) of infra + 1 week ops runbook.
- SCIM/SSO: we can introduce an "immediate revoke" API tied to session service; that is ~1 sprint to implement and 2 weeks for cross-team testing. In the interim we can promise 15-minute TTL in the playbook (but call out residual windows if SCIM events are delayed).

Risk/Blockers: HSM import attestation and legal KYC for key provenance; product needs to agree to the manual UI flag for "short retention." Also need product & legal to sign the exception language for the contract (Ben).

Recommendation: Approve customer onboarding with manual ops for the first pilot (Helio). Schedule infra roadmap items to productize in the next quarter.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: Ops handbook: BYO key flow and SSO risk treatment

Thanks — that helps a lot. I'll consolidate into a short exception playbook and get legal to draft the clause. Proposed immediate plan:

1) Pilot path (Helio): manual BYOK import (wrapped PKCS#8) + manual ops onboarding (2-week lead time). Short-retention account flagged; daily export to Helio S3 for eDiscovery. SCIM clause: 15-minute TTL + emergency revoke API (manual trigger).
2) Product work: UI flag for short-retention + "exception" account routing (1 sprint).
3) Infra work: automate BYOK import & attestation (Q1 next quarter), immediate revoke API (next sprint).
4) Sales/legal: present playbook & exception clause to Helio and Gate exec approval for the credit/terms. Link to HubSpot and DocuSign in related links.

Ben — can you confirm whether Sales is comfortable offering the pilot as "Host+Dedic candidate (Hosted with manual op)" and whether we should include a one-time professional services fee? Also please coordinate a call with Helio security to walk through the playbook.

I'll put a short one-pager together and send for exec review tomorrow.

— Marcus
